title: Rebuild a Tree From Its Text

concept.title: Read the words from left to right with one shared index
body: This is the reverse of the previous problem. The text is the pre-order walk with `#` for missing children. To rebuild the tree, **read the words from left to right** with a shared index and follow the same recursion that wrote them: a `#` is an empty tree; a number is a node, and the text that follows is first its left subtree and then its right subtree.

body.code:
index = 0

def read():
    global index
    word = words[index]
    index += 1
    if word == "#":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(word))
    root.left = read()                       # the left subtree comes first in the text
    root.right = read()
    return root

body: The index must be shared by all calls (a list with one element in Python, a reference in C++, an array of one element in Java), so that after the left subtree is read, the right subtree continues exactly where the left one ended.

statement: A binary tree is written as a pre-order walk where a `#` marks a missing child: a value is a node followed by the text of its left subtree and then the text of its right subtree. Rebuild the tree and print it in level order in the same form as a tree in the input (`N` for a missing child, no `N` at the end).
inputFormat: The first line has `m`, the number of words.

The second line has `m` words: a tree written with the pre-order walk, where `#` stands for a missing child (a value is a node, followed by the text of its left subtree and the text of its right subtree).
outputFormat: The tree in level order on one line.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.
The text is a correct description of a tree.

examples.note: The root 1 has the children 2 and 3: 1 2 3.

hints: Read the words one by one with an index that all calls share.
For a number, create the node, read its left subtree and then its right subtree.

        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.

    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1

        node = queue[head]
        head += 1

            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))

explanation: The words are read once from left to right: # gives an empty tree, a number gives a node whose left and right subtrees are read recursively with the shared index.
